_note: What `code/mailbox.py --file` watches for, minus everything the registry already knows. The watched set is DERIVED at runtime: company hosts from sources/companies.json (`url`, www stripped) go in the replies bucket, board hosts from sources/boards.json go in the alerts bucket, and an ATS relay is watched only when its connector `type` actually appears among enabled connectors - we watch the ATS we apply through, not every ATS that exists. A company added to the registry tomorrow is watched with no edit here. This file holds only the three things that cannot be derived. `via` is the same honesty rule as `domain_via` and `glassdoor_via`: `confirmed` = seen in a real mailbox here, `memory` = written from memory and never observed; a `memory` entry that matches nothing is not a bug.
_alerts_extra_note: Alert senders that are not the board's own host - Indeed and LinkedIn both send from a different domain than the one in boards.json - and every platform whose alert mail is read by its links. `posting` (version 3) is a regex over host+path of ONE posting on that platform, subdomains allowed: a sender with it has every link in its mail unwrapped from click tracking, kept when it matches, and the posting page read for its schema.org JobPosting (mailbox/alerts.ts generic()). A new platform is one row here. `sender` is an address or a host; a host covers every address at it and its subdomains.

_ats_relays_note: connector type -> the domain that ATS sends mail from. All `memory`: none of these has been observed in this mailbox yet, because nothing has been applied to through them. A type not present among enabled connectors is not watched at all.
_exclude_note: Never watched, whatever the registry says. Two kinds. (1) A company you are also a CUSTOMER of - your bank, insurer, telco, railway, supermarket, utility, canton. Their mail is personal, and deriving the watch list from an employer registry is exactly how personal mail would otherwise end up copied into the replies label and parsed into replies.json. (2) A board whose domain also carries non-job mail: linkedin.com and xing.com send messages and network noise from the same host, so only their alert addresses above are watched. Add to this list whenever mail lands in a label that had no business being there - that is cheaper than making the derivation clever.
_replies_exclude_from_note: Senders the REPLIES label never wants, as plain substrings of the address. `exclude` above drops a whole host, which is right for a bank you only bank with and wrong for Google: it is an employer in the registry and its recruiters write from google.com, and so do Play receipts, security alerts and calendar notices. On 2026-09-24 159 of 182 messages in one replies label were that kind of mail. Filing skips these senders (envelope only, no body read) and replies.json drops rows from them, including rows already in the label - Gmail keeps what was copied, since COPY is the only mutation this code has. Alerts are untouched: @jobalert.indeed.com is a real alert, just not a reply.
